Title: Diagnosis of test `survivesPaxHeaderWithNameEndingInSlash`

Details:
The test `survivesPaxHeaderWithNameEndingInSlash` loads a TAR archive from "/COMPRESS-356.tar", expecting it to properly read a single entry named "package/package.json" and then end the stream (no more entries afterward). What it tests is that the code can handle a PAX header with a name ending in a slash correctly.

The sequence of operation as per the `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` method is as follows:
- It reads the header for the next tar entry.
- It constructs a `TarArchiveEntry` from the header.
- If this entry is a GNU long name or link entry, it retrieves the associated long name or link data.
- If it is a global PAX header, it processes the global headers.
- If it is a PAX header (i.e., extended headers), it calls the `paxHeaders()` method.

Within `paxHeaders()`, a map of headers is parsed, and then `getNextEntry()` is called again to move to the actual file entry following the PAX header. After this, the PAX headers are applied to that current entry using `applyPaxHeadersToCurrentEntry()`.

`applyPaxHeadersToCurrentEntry()` applies values from the headers to the current entry, including name changes from the "path" header key.

When the name is set on the entry via `currEntry.setName(val)`, it normalizes the file name by calling `normalizeFileName(String name, boolean preserveLeadingSlashes)`. This method:
- Strips drive letters if on Windows and network drive prefixes on Netware.
- Replaces system-specific file separators with '/'.
- Strips leading slashes unless `preserveLeadingSlashes` is true.

The primary cause of failure for the test may be related to how the normalization in `setName` removes or modifies trailing slashes or the details of how PAX header names ending with a slash are handled. The test expects the resulting entry to have the name "package/package.json" (no trailing slash), but a PAX header with a name ending in a slash might not be normalized or applied correctly, leading to a mismatch or skipping of entries.

Thus, the bug likely resides around the processing and normalization of PAX header names with trailing slashes in:
- How `paxHeaders()` triggers fetching the actual entry and applying headers.
- How `applyPaxHeadersToCurrentEntry` handles "path" keys with trailing slashes.
- How `setName` normalizes names, potentially removing important trailing slashes or otherwise mishandling the name.

The failure indicates the entry name is not what is expected after applying pax headers, possibly due to a trailing slash in the pax header "path" name that is not properly normalized or filtered out.

Suggested methods to fix:
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.paxHeaders()
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.applyPaxHeadersToCurrentEntry(java.util.Map)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry.setName(java.lang.String)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry.normalizeFileName(java.lang.String, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
